article.title: Extension functions in C++/PHP
article.p: This section describes how to extend the capability of Saxon XSLT stylesheets and XQuery queries by adding user written extension functions in the C++, Python and PHP languages.

Extension functions allow code written in a host programming language such as C++, Python and PHP to be invoked directly from a function call in an XPath expression (whether in XSLT, XQuery, or pure XPath). For this to work the Saxon processor needs to be able to locate the executable code corresponding to a particular function name. For the function arguments these can be as XDM types or converted to the host language type system, with the opposite conversion applied to the function result.

XSLT, XQuery, and XPath are functional languages where it is assumed that functions do not have side effects. Saxon cannot stop you calling extension functions that have side effects, but the effect of doing so is not always guaranteed. For example, the optimizer might eliminate a call to an extension function whose results are never used, or it might execute calls to extension functions in an unexpected order.

Allowing untrusted stylesheets or queries to call extension functions is a potential security risk. Stylesheets and queries will only be able to call extension functions that have been explicitly registered by the application; it is the responsibility of the application designer to ensure that this does not create vulnerabilities.

To register a user defined function SaxonC needs to know the signature of any function that it might call. The signature tells the processor the name of each function that can be called, the number and types pf its arguments. and the expected return type.
SaxonC provides a new API for registering extension functions. This registration must be done before any attempt is made to evaluate an expression or compile an XSLT stylesheet that uses one.

The SaxonProcessor class in the SaxonC API contains for this purpose the registerUserFunction(apiDescription) method, which takes a JSON string of the user's function. This method exists on the C++, Python and PHP APIs for SaxonC.
The apiDescription argument is a map of the following form:
The namespace identifies the function namespace, the local name of the function identifies the function name which maps to the signature of the function. The signature has four properties:

tr.td: The return type, an XML Schema data type, for example xs:boolean.
The parameter types, one for each parameter, as an XML Schema data type.

The function arities. In the common case, this is just an array of length one containing the arity of the function. If the function can be called with multiple arities, this is a list of the arities that can be used, for example [1, 3, 4] for a function that can be called with one, three, or four arguments.

article.p: When compiling a stylesheet (with the SaxonCEE compiler), the registered extension functions are provided in a JSON object using SaxonProcessor.registerUserFunction(apiDescription).
article.h2: Function argument and return type conversions
article.p: As mentioned above, when an XDM item is passed to the user function in the host language (i.e. C++, PHP or Python), it can be passed as an XDM type or for Python and PHP the item can be converted into the Python or PHP representation, respectively. Conversely, when a function wants to return a value, it can either be returned as an XDM type or a Python/PHP representation that can be converted back into an XDM type. We discuss these in more detail for each host language in SaxonC.
For general information about extension functions, see Extension functions.
To write extension functions in C++, see Extension functions (C++).
To write extension functions in PHP, see Extension functions (PHP).
To write extension functions in Python, see Extension functions (Python).

section.title: Writing extension functions in C++
section.p: A full example of the use of extension functions can be found in the files testXPath.cpp in the samples/cppTest directory. This sample test registers a user written C++ extension function called "myFunc". Arguments and return types of User functions written in C++ can only be XDM types. This is different to Python and PHP which can handle native types.

Example C++ code to register user function:
SaxonProcessor * processor = new SaxonProcessor(true); processor->registerUserFunction("http://www.example.com", &myFunc, "{ \"myFunc\": {" " \"as\": \"xs:integer\"," " \"param\": [" " \"xs:integer\"" " ]," " \"arity\": [1]" " }" "}");

Notice that the registration of the user function in C++ that we pass the function as a void pointer to the registerUserFunction method. This is essential for the call-back mechanism. The arguments must also have the signature (int length, XdmValue* arguments). The length argument is the number of arguments being passed to the function from the SaxonC processor. The arguments are tjhe inputs to the user function. In C++ we only accept arguments of XDM types.

section.title: Writing extension functions in PHP
section.p: Examples of the User extension functions in PHP are found in the sample file userFunctionTest.php in the samples/php directory. The PHP file contains a variety of examples illustrating the capabilities of the feature.

For the registering of a user function we use the SaxonProcessor method registerUserFunction:
registerUserFunction(string ns, string json, bool useNativeTypes)

User extension functions in PHP can both handle arguments of XDM and native PHP types. The same for the return type from the function. The boolean flag useNativeTypes=True on registerUserFunction is used to switch on native type conversion option. This means that users can use native PHP types within the function they have written and return them too. If useNativeTypes=False means we are only handling XDM types. XdmNode types does not have a native type mapping. Therefore, we just pass arguments of this type to the user function.

Mapping of XDM types to native PHP types:
XdmNode -> XdmNode - No conversion
XdmFunctionItem -> XdmXdmFunctionItem - No conversion
XdmArray -> Array
XdmMap -> Array with keys from the XdmMap
XdmValue (sequence) -> ArrayIterator
EmptySequence -> NULL
XdmAtomicValue:
Xdm int types -> Integer
Xdm double type (inc decimal, float) -> Float
Xdm double type (inc decimal) -> Float
Xdm boolean -> Boolean
All other XdmAtomic types -> String
The return types works in the same mapping in reverse. If the user chooses to convert sequence type (i.e. an XdmValue) to a native type this will be done as an ArrayIterator. For the return value to interpret an XdmValue from a native type the user must create an ArrayIterator object.

Example PHP code to register user function:
$saxonProc = new Saxon\SaxonProcessor(true); $xpath = $saxonProc->newXPathProcessor(); $saxonProc->registerUserFunction("http://www.example.com", "{ \"sumASequence\": {". " \"as\": \"xs:integer?\"," . " \"param\": [" . " \"array(xs:integer*)\"" . " ],". " \"arity\": [1]" . " }". "}", True);

section.title: Writing extension functions in Python
section.p: Examples of the User extension functions feature in Python are found in the pytests file test_saxonc.py in the pypi directory.

For the registering of a user function we use the PySaxonProcessor method register_user_function:
register_user_function(string ns, func, string json, encoding=None, use_python_types=False)

User extension functions in Python can both handle arguments of XDM and native PHP types. The same for the return type from the function. The boolean flag use_python_types=True on register_user_function is used to switch on native type conversion option. This means that users can use native PHP types within the function they have written and return them too. The default option is use_python_types=False. which means we are only handling XDM types in the user function. XdmNode types does not have a native type mapping. Therefore, we just pass arguments of this type to the user function.

Mapping of XDM types to native PHP types:
PyXdmNode -> PyXdmNode - No conversion
PyXdmFunctionItem -> PyXdmXdmFunctionItem - No conversion
PyXdmArray -> list
PyXdmMap -> dict
PyXdmValue (sequence) -> iter??
PyXdmAtomicValue:
Xdm int types -> int
Xdm double type (inc decimal, float) -> float
Xdm double type (inc decimal) -> Float
Xdm boolean -> bool
All other XdmAtomic types -> str
The return types works in the same mapping in reverse. If the user chooses to convert sequence type (i.e. an PyXdmValue) to a native type this will be done as an iter. For the return value to interpret an PyXdmValue from a native type the user must create an iter object.

Example Python code to register user function:
proc.register_user_function("http://www.example.com", user_function, "{ \"myFunc\": {" " \"as\": \"xs:integer?\"," " \"param\": [" " \"xs:integer\"" " ]," " \"arity\": [1]" " }" "}", use_python_types=False)
